events.title: The Special Period begins
events.detail: Following the collapse of Soviet trade and subsidies, Cuba declared a peacetime emergency, rationing fuel and food and later legalising the dollar, self-employment and foreign joint ventures.
events.contested: Output fell by around a third in four years. Health and education indicators held up far better than income, which is read either as evidence that social provision can be insulated from economic collapse, or as a question about how those indicators are measured and reported.
events.refs: ["Mesa-Lago, 'Growing Economic and Social Disparities in Cuba' (2002)"]

events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 11%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 4,961 to 4,395 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.
